messages:
maria.g: FYI ran a couple of tests after landing the fused-attn kernel. Seeing small but consistent log-prob drift when using ROPE-based models at fp16. Not huge, but reproduces on our long-seq regression suite.

sam.h: How small? percent-wise or absolute token-level?

maria.g: ~0.2-0.6% on log-prob averaged across prompts; spikes larger for seq_len>2048. Happens only with the new fused kernel + mixed-precision path. CPU/FP32 path is clean.

kevin.w: Do we have concrete reproducer? deterministic seed + model + input?

maria.g: Yep. Pushing a minimal repro gists: 

```
model: redwood/rotary-8b-test
seq_len: 4096
precision: fp16
kernel: fused-attn-v2
seed: 42
command: python -m tests.repro --model ...
```

kevin.w: Got it. I can try bisecting kernel changes. Could be accumulation order or a blended scaling factor.

anya.r: Another signal — similar drift on ALiBi when we enable buffer-packing + int8 kv cache. Not identical but suggests positional encoding math interacting poorly with precision/packing.

sam.h: Two orthogonal dimensions: (1) positional encoding implementation (ROPE vs ALiBi) and (2) kernel execution path (fused vs fallback + packing/quant). Need to decide interface boundary: kernel should get already-normalized sin/cos? or raw q/k and apply posenc internally? Right now different kernels expect different inputs.

maria.g: Exactly. Today our kernel selector switches implementations but relies on caller to pass q/k in the kernel-specific layout. That means positional math sometimes happens pre-kernel in fp32 then cast, other times inside kernel in fp16. Inconsistent.

kevin.w: That's a likely source. Casting after applying ROPE in fp32 vs applying in fp16 inside kernel will produce different results. We should pick a clear contract: either always apply posenc before quantization/call or always inside kernel with fixed precision.

sam.h: Proposal: define a PosEncContract: callers always pass raw q/k (no posenc applied). Kernels must implement posenc application and be responsible for numerically-stable variants under a requested precision flag (fp32/fp16/amp). Add fallback to caller-side posenc if kernel advertises 'no-posenc' capability.

anya.r: That moves complexity into kernels but centralizes behavior which sounds right for consistency. Also we can version capabilities so runtime can fall back.

maria.g: For short-term patch (low-risk): add test that compares outcomes of (a) caller-applied ROPE-fp32 then cast->kernel vs (b) kernel-applied ROPE-fp16. If mismatch > epsilon -> force fallback to fp32 kernel for that model/sequence. This will mitigate customer regressions while we refactor.

kevin.w: I can implement the test harness. Question: what epsilon threshold? absolute log-prob delta or relative?

sam.h: Use both: delta_logprob > 0.001 absolute OR relative > 0.5% flagged. Tunable. Document reasons.

maria.g: Also noticed that our fused kernel uses an in-kernel pre-scaling step: multiply q by inv_sqrt_d, then apply sin/cos. The original math applies ROPE on unscaled q then scale later. Order may matter in fp16.

kevin.w: Right. Reordering ops in fp16 affects rounding. We should align op order to reference implementation. Option: use compensated scaling (Kahan-like) or do some ops in fp32 internally (accumulate in fp32 then cast).

anya.r: For ALiBi, the linear bias addition can be tiny relative to token logits after scaling which underflows in fp16. We could introduce a staged add in fp32 for the bias only.

sam.h: Action items I propose: 
- short-term: add the regression flagging test + fallback to fp32 for flagged model-config combos (maria + kevin)
- mid-term: RFC to define PosEncContract and kernel capability flags (anya)
- mid-term: update kernel selector to consider (model.posenc_type, seq_len, requested_precision, kernel_capabilities) (sam)
- long-term: refactor kernels to expose numerically-stable codepaths + unit tests with synthetic edge cases (kevin)

kevin.w: I'll open a PR for the harness and a small selector tweak to prefer fp32 for seq_len>2048 until we finish the refactor.

maria.g: I'll compile a short reproducibility doc with the exact prompts and seed, include perf numbers (latency/cost regression if we force fp32 fallback) so product/ops understand tradeoffs.

anya.r: I'll draft the PosEncContract RFC. Suggest we include: input layout expectations, precision guarantees, fallback semantics, and a small test matrix for ROPE/ALiBi/other posenc variants.

ci-bot: build/1774002245 - fused-attn-v2 CI passed :white_check_mark: (linux-gpu, tests: 312/312)

sam.h: CI passed but doesn't exercise long-seq floats. We'll need expanded tests in nightly suite.

maria.g: Noted perf hit when forcing fp32: +18% tail latency for 4096 seq on p4. We'll add telemetry to surface when fallbacks occur so SLOs can be tracked.

kevin.w: Quick note: check kv-cache packing semantics. If we quantize cached kv in int8, applying posenc after quantization is impossible. Need to ensure posenc is applied to raw float k before any irreversible quant/pack. That enforces ordering constraint.

sam.h: Good call. Add to RFC: 'posenc must be applied before irreversible packing/quantization' unless kernel advertises 'posenc-with-packing' capability with strict tests.

anya.r: Sounds like consensus. I'll start RFC draft and post link here.

maria.g: Posting repro gist in thread: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-rotary-drift

kevin.w: I'll pick this up after stand. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam.h: Let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to align on selector changes and rollout plan.

anya.r: Adding agenda: examples, RFC outline, metric thresholds for fallback.

ci-bot: deploy/1774002500 - canary deploy started for fused-attn-v2 (region: us-west2)

maria.g: I'll monitor canary logs for posenc-fallback occurrences and post updates.

kevin.w: If we see high fallback rate, we should consider a staged flag to revert to previous kernel for affected models.

sam.h: Agreed. End-to-end plan looks good. Thanks team.
